nodes.name: Schedule_Trigger_5Min
nodes.notes: Processes pending and failed-but-retryable Calendar integration operations every 5 minutes.

parameters.query:
-- Claim integration operations using safe lease semantics (finding #15)
-- Uses claim_integration_operations() which:
--   1. Supersedes obsolete operations (GCAL_UPDATE/DELETE replaces older ones)
--   2. Auto-marks already-satisfied operations as SUCCESS
--   3. Claims remaining operations with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
--   4. Sets lease_expires_at = NOW() + 10 minutes for crash recovery
--   5. Increments attempt_count (but not for IN_PROGRESS recovery)
--
-- Joins with appointments and doctors to provide all context needed by Calendar Worker.
WITH claimed AS (
    SELECT * FROM claim_integration_operations(
        p_batch_size    := 10,
        p_lease_minutes := 10
    )
)
SELECT
    c.operation_id,
    c.appointment_id,
    c.operation_type,
    c.attempt_count,
    c.max_attempts,
    c.idempotency_key,
    c.lease_expires_at,
    c.payload,
    a.customer_name,
    a.service,
    a.start_time,
    a.end_time,
    a.status AS appt_status,
    a.calendar_event_id,
    a.appointment_source,
    d.doctor_name,
    d.calendar_id,
    d.timezone
FROM claimed c
JOIN appointments a ON c.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
JOIN doctors d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id;

-- Mark integration operation as SUCCESS and update appointment's calendar_event_id
-- Called after any successful GCal operation (CREATE, UPDATE, or DELETE).
-- finding #16: This is the "before DB success update" crash point.
-- The claim_integration_operations() function pre-checks for already-synced
-- appointments (calendar_event_id already set), so reaching here means
-- the GCal operation genuinely just succeeded.

-- Set actor for audit trail
SELECT set_config('app.current_actor', 'system:calendar_worker', true);

WITH op_update AS (
    UPDATE integration_operations
    SET status = 'SUCCESS',
        lease_expires_at = NULL,
        updated_at = NOW()
    WHERE operation_id = $1
    RETURNING operation_id, appointment_id, operation_type
),
appt_update AS (
    UPDATE appointments a
    SET
        -- For CREATE/UPDATE: store the new event_id
        -- For DELETE: clear the event_id (event no longer exists)
        calendar_event_id = CASE
            WHEN o.operation_type = 'GCAL_DELETE'
                THEN NULL
            WHEN o.operation_type IN ('GCAL_CREATE', 'GCAL_UPDATE')
                 AND $2 IS NOT NULL AND $2 != ''
                THEN $2
            ELSE a.calendar_event_id
        END,
        updated_at = NOW()
    FROM op_update o
    WHERE a.appointment_id = o.appointment_id
    RETURNING a.appointment_id, a.calendar_event_id, o.operation_type
)
SELECT * FROM appt_update;

-- Mark operation as FAILED or PERMANENTLY_FAILED based on attempt_count vs max_attempts
-- Implements exponential backoff for retry (finding #15)
UPDATE integration_operations
SET
    status = CASE
        WHEN attempt_count >= max_attempts THEN 'PERMANENTLY_FAILED'
        ELSE 'FAILED'
    END,
    lease_expires_at = NULL,
    next_retry_at = CASE
        WHEN attempt_count < max_attempts
        THEN NOW() + (INTERVAL '1 minute' * POWER(2, LEAST(attempt_count, 10)))
        ELSE NULL
    END,
    error_details = $1::jsonb,
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE operation_id = $2
RETURNING operation_id, status, attempt_count, max_attempts, next_retry_at;

nodes.name: Maintenance_Trigger_Hourly
nodes.notes: Runs maintenance tasks every hour: expire stale PENDING appointments, clean up old processed_messages. Separated from customer request path (finding #109, #110).

parameters.query:
-- Maintenance: expire stale PENDING appointments (finding #109)
-- These cleanup tasks run SEPARATELY from customer requests (finding #110)
-- expire_stale_pending_appointments() internally sets app.current_actor = 'system:maintenance'
SELECT
    expire_stale_pending_appointments() AS expired_appointments,
    cleanup_old_processed_messages(7)   AS deleted_messages;
